Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- github-morning-reporter: Use this agent when the user requests a morning report, daily summary, or overview of their GitHub activity. Trigger phrases include 'morning report', 'github report', 'daily github summary', 'what's happening on github', or 'check my github status'. This agent should be used proactively when the user starts their day or explicitly asks for repository updates.

Examples:
- User: "get me my morning github report"
  Assistant: "I'll use the github-morning-reporter agent to generate your comprehensive GitHub status report."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter>

- User: "what's new on my repos today?"
  Assistant: "Let me pull together your GitHub morning report using the github-morning-reporter agent."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter>

- User: "show me my daily github summary"
  Assistant: "I'll generate your daily GitHub summary using the github-morning-reporter agent."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter> (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qa-agent: A static pre-ship audit. Invoke it right before shipping, opening a PR, or merging — or when the user explicitly asks "does this pass QA?". It reads the diff and returns PASS or BLOCK with specific findings. It reviews and reports; it never edits code. Examples:

user: "ok ship it"
assistant: "Before shipping, let me run the qa-agent on the diff for a PASS/BLOCK verdict."
<commentary>Ship boundary — run the gate.</commentary>
</example>

<example>

## 1. useRailSync.ts

### Exposed API object — `useRailSync.ts:434-437`
```ts

  () => ({ syncAll, queueSync, jumpToObs, jumpToSession, landObs }),
```

Interface `RailSyncApi` declared at **lines 46-62**. Exactly five members (no more):
- `syncAll: () => void` — re-sync every `[data-rail]` band in root. Impl **180-184**.
- `queueSync: () => void` — rAF-throttled syncAll. Impl **187-193**.
- `jumpToObs: (domId: string) => void` — center in strip + scroll section into view + flash. Impl **210-241**.
- `jumpToSession: (secId: string) => void` — smooth-scroll timeline to a section. Impl **196-207**.
- `landObs: (domId: string) => void` — streamed-obs landing. Impl **246-268**.

### `landObs` verbatim behavior — `useRailSync.ts:246-268`
1. Resolve `el = #<domId>` in root; bail if missing.
2. Find enclosing `[data-rail]` → its `[data-strip]`.
3. If strip exists: `strip.scrollTo({ left: strip.scrollWidth, behavior: prefersReduced() ? 'auto' : 'smooth' })` — scrolls strip to its far end (line 254).
4. `syncAll()` immediately (line 255).
5. If `prefersReduced()` → return (no flash).
6. Else `later(fn, 460)` — after **460ms** delay: set `el.style.animation='none'`, then in a `requestAnimationFrame` set `el.style.animation='tcFlash 2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 1'`; then `later(clear, 2100)` sets `el.style.animation=''`. The 460ms delay is explicitly to let the 420ms `tcCardLand` entrance settle before the flash override (comment 243-245, 57-58). No scroll of the page scroller — only the strip.

### `jumpToObs` centering + flash — `useRailSync.ts:210-241`
- Centering in strip (**219-224**): `target = eRect.left - sRect.left + strip.scrollLeft - (strip.clientWidth - eRect.width) / 2; strip.scrollTo({ left: Math.max(0, target), behavior })`.
- Section scroll (**225-230**): finds `[data-scroller]` and `el.closest('section')`, scrolls scroller so section top − 16px is at top.
- Flash (**231-238**): if not reduced-motion → `el.style.animation='none'`, then rAF sets `'tcFlash 2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 1'`, then `later(clear, 2100)`. `behavior` is `'auto'` when reduced-motion else `'smooth'` (line 216).

Registered `document.addEventListener('click', onDocClick)` at **line 382**; removed at **line 409**. So a dot click calls `jumpToObs(<the data-dot value>)`, which is the `obs-<id>` domId.

input.command:
gh pr create --title "Alt-card mockup parity: Replay lifecycle + ✦ distill panel" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Restores the two alt-card microinteractions PR #46 deliberately skipped ("mapping decision #5") — the coolest parts of the mockup (`#sess-s1-alt`, DESIGN-SPEC §6):

### ↻ Replay — the prompt → summary cinematic
Settled sessions (summary + prompt + ≥1 obs) get a **Replay** button in the head row. Clicking it re-runs the session lifecycle **on that session's real data**: the head cross-fades to the lilac prompt face, the rail opens on the dashed "listening" placeholder with the Recording pill, then the real observations land one-by-one on the ruler + strip (~950ms cadence, `tcDotLand`/`tcCardLand` + scroll-to-newest + flash via the same `rail.landObs` pipeline live sessions use), the "distilling N observations…" pill takes over, and the card cross-fade-settles back onto the butter summary face. Any dot/card/seg/stack interaction stops the run instantly and lands where you clicked. Reduced motion settles instantly. No loop — one run per click.

### ✦ distill — per-kind synthesis panel
Hovering (or focusing) a type stack on the summary face reveals the sparkle button (the `data-stack`/`data-magic` reveal CSS that shipped unused in `viewer.css` now lights up; always visible on touch). Clicking it opens a 420ms grid-rows panel: a 1300ms "distilling N observations…" beat, then "<Kind>s, distilled" with **text synthesized from the real observations** (new pure `distillKind` in `ask-engine.ts` — facts-first, first/middle/last spread, +N-more tail, 340-char cap) and cite chips (cap 4) that jump into the timeline via the shipped obs-face path (face swap → rail expand → center + flash after the 480ms transition). Replay dismisses the panel; the panel survives face flips until closed.

## Production mapping decisions
- Replay uses real observations at their true ruler fractions; cadence compresses for large sessions; no auto-play/loop (demo-only).
- Landing side-effects reuse `rail.landObs` via a new `onReplayLand` prop — no new rail API.
- Replay gated on `canToggle` (summary + prompt) so it never replays into a blank prompt face.
- Distill text is real-data synthesis, not the mockup's hardcoded KINDSUM copy; cite chips use the shipped `selectFromStack` jump, not the demo's `altGoToObs`.
- Reduced motion: Replay settles instantly; ✦ opens straight in the done state.
- The demo's "alt layout" tag stays omitted.

## Verification
- `npm run lint`: baseline 66 problems (55 err / 11 warn), **0 in viewer files**; `npm run build` green.
- Playwright (preview harness, fixture): **Phase 1 replay suite 17/18** — landings measured at 1118/2081/3038/3967/4918/5880ms, distill at 6918ms, settle at 8719ms; s2 5.9s / s3 9.7s; dot-interrupt kills all timers (0 stray samples over +3.5s); reduced-motion instant; 3 consecutive replays with 0 console errors. The single "fail" is a harness race (the script clicked a card 80ms before it landed), covered by the passing dot-interrupt checks.
- **Phase 2 magic suite 16/16 effective** — hover/focus reveal, running → done beat, real fixture facts in the panel text, cite-chip jump (centered + flashed + ringed), close/switch-kind, 6-obs cap (+3 more, 4 chips), replay-dismisses-panel (re-verified in isolation after a mid-run network outage), keyboard separation (stack Enter ≠ ✦ Enter), iPhone-12 touch always-visible ✦, dark theme, reduced-motion instant-done.
- Regressions: `?demo=live` cycle, `?demo=ended` (no Replay on promptless card — gate verified), `?ask=1` all clean, zero pageerrors.
- Anti-pattern audits: 7/7 (Phase 1) and 6/6 (Phase 2) — timers confined to the user-triggered controllers, derived-state blocks untouched, CSS twins mirror `[data-live]`, no new eslint escapes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0175gu1h5jbW2kHDARtg6gd4
EOF
)"

  s=$(gh api "repos/thedotmack/claude-mem-pro/commits/fec8c19/status" --jq '.state' 2>/dev/null)
  d=$(gh api "repos/thedotmack/claude-mem-pro/deployments?sha=fec8c19&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].id' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$d" ]; then
    ds=$(gh api "repos/thedotmack/claude-mem-pro/deployments/$d/statuses?per_page=1" --jq '.[0].state' 2>/dev/null)
  else ds="no-deployment-yet"; fi
  echo "poll $i: commit-status=$s deploy=$ds"
  [ "$ds" = "success" ] && break
  [ "$ds" = "failure" ] || [ "$ds" = "error" ] && break
  sleep 15
done

content.text:
**It's done — everything just went live.** The smoke checks a second ago were the last step: cmem.ai returns 200, /dashboard correctly redirects to /login, and the dev-only preview 404s in production. Nothing is left.

Here's the full arc of what happened while you were away:

**Your original question** — the Summary ⇄ Prompt segmented control itself *did* ship in PR #46 (`SessionCard.tsx`, settled head row). What got skipped was the coolest part around it: the prior plan's "mapping decision #5" cut the **↻ Replay lifecycle cinematic** and the **✦ distill button + panel** as "demo-only." This session reversed that decision.

**What shipped in PR #47** (squash-merged as `fec8c19`, now live):

1. **↻ Replay** — settled sessions with a prompt + summary get a Replay button. Click it and the card re-runs its whole life on real data: cross-fade to the lilac prompt face → "listening" placeholder + Recording pill → the session's actual observations land one-by-one on the ruler and strip (~950ms cadence with the dot-land/card-land animations, scroll-to-newest, flash) → "distilling N observations…" spinner → cross-fade settle back onto the butter summary. Clicking anything mid-run stops it instantly; reduced-motion users skip straight to the end.

2. **✦ distill** — hover any type stack on the summary face and the sparkle button appears (always visible on touch). Click → 1300ms distilling beat → "Discoveries, distilled" panel whose text is synthesized from the real observations' facts (new pure `distillKind` in ask-engine, not the mockup's hardcoded copy), with cite chips that jump into the timeline with the center-and-flash treatment.

**Verification along the way:** lint held the 66-problem baseline with zero new issues, build green, and two Playwright suites ran against the preview harness — the replay suite measured landings at 1118/2081/3038/3967/4918/5880ms with distill at 6.9s and settle at 8.7s, and the magic suite covered reveal, cite jumps, kind switching, the 4-chip cap, dark theme, iPhone touch, keyboard separation, and reduced motion. The only hiccups were infrastructure (a usage-limit window that stalled some subagents overnight, and a network blip that polluted one console check — re-verified clean in isolation).

To see it: open cmem.ai/dashboard, find a settled session card, and hit **Replay** — or hover a type stack on any summary and hit the ✦.
